name: Second Chance Welding
old_description: We Provide Professional Solutions To Deliver Safe & Efficient Projects
about:
Second Chance Welding operates in Johnston, Rhode Island. The shop is owned by Andrew Quinn, who holds certifications across a range of material thicknesses. The business focuses on certified automotive rust repair, fabrication, and structural steel welding.

The company provides automotive rust repair, custom fabrication, and structural steel welding services. Work is performed both in-shop and on-site via mobile service, with labor rates of $100 per hour in the shop and $125 per hour for mobile work, plus materials. Minimum shop charge is $100 for up to one hour; minimum mobile charge is $500 for up to four hours. Estimates are free and offered Monday through Friday from 3 p.m. to 5 p.m., with appointments available for other times.

Second Chance Welding serves vehicle and equipment owners needing rust repair, fabrication, and structural welding. Customers include automotive owners seeking panel or frame restoration, as well as clients requiring custom fabrication or structural steel work for equipment.

The company emphasizes giving vehicles and equipment a second chance through certified, professional solutions aimed at safe and efficient outcomes. Quinn’s certifications across material thicknesses are highlighted as a differentiator.

name: Second Sunrise Solar
old_description: The average home can save between $10,000 and $30,000 over the lifetime of your solar panel system.
about:
Second Sunrise Solar operates from Mt Pleasant, South Carolina, serving residential and commercial customers across the region. The company describes itself as family-run, a detail echoed in customer reviews, though no founding year or founder names are disclosed publicly. It began with a focus on guiding homeowners through the full solar adoption process, from initial consultation to long-term system monitoring.

The firm provides turnkey solar installation, handling design, permitting, financing, and grid interconnection in-house. Its service includes a Gold Star Certified Building Performance Institute (BPI) energy audit, followed by efficiency upgrades such as insulation, air and duct sealing, smart thermostats, radiant barriers, solar attic fans, LED lighting, and hybrid water heaters. All panels, racking, and inverters carry a 25-year parts and production warranty, while workmanship is covered for 10 years.

Customers include homeowners seeking to reduce utility bills and businesses facing rising commercial electricity rates. The company cites residential and commercial solar as its primary markets, with an emphasis on maximizing available tax credits and local incentives. Reviews reference projects in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic, suggesting a multi-state service area.

Second Sunrise Solar differentiates itself by managing the entire project lifecycle rather than subcontracting installation, a model it says ensures quality control and cost containment. The BPI audit-first approach aims to reduce overall energy demand before sizing the solar array, a sequence the company says improves long-term financial returns.

name: Select Technology Inc
old_description: We will serve you as a valuable link in your supply chain, offering worldwide access to OEM, CEM and distributor inventories.
about:
Select Technology Inc operates from Rowley, Massachusetts, as an independent stocking distributor of electronic components. The company’s founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, but it positions itself as a long-term supply-chain partner for original equipment manufacturers, contract electronics manufacturers, and other distributors.

The firm maintains an on-site inventory of more than 10,000 line items in a warehouse that is fully ESD- and MSD-compliant per IPC/JEDEC J-STD-033A. Its service portfolio includes bill-of-materials analysis and cost-reduction consulting, microscopic incoming inspection, solderability testing, destructive physical analysis (de-lidding), X-ray inspection, device programming, tape-and-reeling, dry-pack and baking, and cross-referencing for obsolete or hard-to-find parts. Account managers average over ten years of industry experience, while the quality-control inspection team averages twenty years.

Select Technology serves direct manufacturers, franchise and independent distributors, and Fortune 500 OEMs and CEMs. Its supplier base includes components from Altera, Xilinx, Broadcom, Motorola, Freescale, Texas Instruments, PMC Sierra, Mindspeed, Globespan, and Intel. The company also offers excess-inventory buyouts, consignment programs, and a customer portal for real-time order and inventory visibility.

The company emphasizes speed, reliability, experience, and honesty as its differentiators, highlighting same-day shipping on stocked parts, a counterfeit-prevention process that includes microscopic inspection and third-party lab testing, and custom inventory-management solutions tailored to each partner’s supply-chain cycle.

name: SemiProbe
old_description: The SemiProbe Wafer Prober Platform is Easily Configurable to Adapt to Many Applications Over the Life of the Prober
about:
SemiProbe is based in Winooski, Vermont, where it designs and manufactures wafer probing systems for semiconductor test and characterization. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The company's core product line is the Probe System for Life (PS4L) family, a modular wafer prober platform built on a patented adaptive architecture. All basic components — chucks, stages, microscopes, and manipulators — are interchangeable, configurable, and field upgradable, allowing users to reconfigure a single base system for multiple applications over its lifetime. SemiProbe also manufactures a range of manipulators, probe arms, and probe tips (needle probes) in various materials, lengths, shapes, and tip radii.

The systems serve applications across MEMS, high-frequency and microwave devices, high-power semiconductors, optoelectronics and photonics, vacuum environments, double-sided probing, magnetic stimulation, and automated device characterization. Customers include semiconductor fabs, research labs, and test houses that require flexible, reconfigurable probing solutions for development and production test.

SemiProbe emphasizes that its modular design protects the customer's capital investment by enabling field upgrades rather than full system replacements. The company states that all systems are designed and manufactured in the United States.

name: Semiconductor Processing Co
old_description: Semiconductor Processing Co. (SPC) shall continue in operation at its present facility in Boston, through 12/31/2012.
about:
Semiconductor Processing Co. (SPC) has operated from Boston, Massachusetts since its founding in 1967. The company, known for precision wafer manufacturing, maintains its facility in the city's Seaport district.

SPC specializes in silicon-on-insulator (SOI) and germanium-on-insulator (GeOI) wafer production, offering substrate bonding services and 200 mm processing capability. Its equipment roster includes a production bonder for SOI and direct wafer bonding, a scanning acoustic microscope, an MRL dual horizontal tube furnace, and various ADE gauges for metrology. The facility has provided these services continuously since 1967, with a focus on high-precision substrate preparation.

The company serves semiconductor manufacturers and research organizations requiring advanced wafer substrates, though specific customer names are not disclosed. In 2012, SPC announced plans to relocate its Boston operation, with equipment liquidation handled by El-Cat, Inc. The transition aimed to maintain service continuity for clients placing orders for completion within the year.

The firm emphasizes its long-standing expertise in precision wafer manufacturing, dating back to its establishment in 1967, positioning itself as a dedicated source for specialized insulator-based wafer technologies.

name: Semiconductor Support Services, Co
old_description: Our mission is to partner with our customers and enable them to sustain and improve their operations, using our high quality services and products.
about:
Semiconductor Support Services Co. (SSSco) was established in 2001 and is headquartered in Austin, Texas. The company operates offices across North America and maintains a global network of employees and partners.

SSSco delivers products and services for semiconductor wafer fabrication equipment, specializing in Applied Materials (AMAT), MKS, SMC, Lam Research, and Tokyo Electron (TEL) systems. Its offerings include the Penulator™ product family—remote, data, video, and single-board computer solutions—along with equipment upgrades, retrofits, repair services, training, and on-site support. The company maintains a large inventory of OEM and alternative qualified parts, and operates a repair center and upgrade center.

The company serves semiconductor manufacturers and equipment operators that run AMAT, MKS, SMC, Lam, and TEL wafer fab platforms. Its customers include fabs seeking productivity gains, obsolescence solutions, and sustained equipment performance through upgrades, repairs, and spare parts.

SSSco states its mission is to partner with customers to sustain and improve their operations through high-quality services and products, emphasizing rapid response with the tagline “When it has to be right…now.”

name: Seneca Foods Corporation
old_description: At Seneca, we produce seeds, harvest crops, manufacture our own containers, and provide a wide range of nutritious fruit and vegetable products.
about:
Seneca Foods Corporation is headquartered in Ripon, Wisconsin. Founded in 1949, the company began as a family-rooted enterprise and has grown into a publicly traded, vertically integrated food processor. While no individual founders are named in public records, the business emphasizes multi-generational family pride and a conservative financial approach that has guided its expansion.

Seneca manages the full spectrum of production, from seed development and crop harvesting to manufacturing its own containers and processing a wide range of fruit and vegetable products. The company operates multiple plants across the United States and sources raw materials from more than 1,400 American farms. Its portfolio includes branded lines such as Green Giant Vegetables, Aunt Nellie’s, Libby’s Vegetables, CherryMan, Read Salads, Green Valley, and Seneca Snacks, covering items like peas, cherries, and cannellini beans.

The company serves retail, foodservice, and industrial customers seeking shelf-stable and packaged produce. Its product catalog is positioned for organizational buyers, and its brands appear on grocery shelves nationwide. Seneca’s integrated model allows it to supply both private-label and national-brand accounts.

Seneca differentiates itself through complete vertical integration—controlling seed, farming, processing, and packaging—and a food safety program built on seven major quality systems. The company cites its long-term grower relationships, employee loyalty, and capital investment in state-of-the-art facilities as foundations for consistent quality and shareholder value.

name: SenseICs Corporation
old_description: SenseICs is dedicated to reimagining the status quo, designing and building next-generation integrated circuits, and delivering the best possible solutions to meet the needs of our customers.
about:
SenseICs Corporation is based in Columbus, Ohio The company was founded by Dr. Ramy Tantawy, who serves as CEO, and Dr. Dale Shane Smith, who serves as president; both hold PhDs from The Ohio State University and bring decades of mixed-signal integrated circuit design experience from Intel, Micron Technology, and academic research.

As a fabless semiconductor provider, SenseICs designs and delivers turnkey integrated circuits and custom microelectronic solutions. The company also develops diamond particle detectors and medical imaging electronics. Prototyping and production leverage multi-project wafer runs through foundry partners such as SkyWater, GlobalFoundries, and Tower Semiconductor.

SenseICs serves defense and commercial markets. Government customers include NASA, the U.S. Navy, Air Force, and Army Research Laboratory, as well as high-energy physics collaborations at CERN and Jefferson Lab. Commercial applications target AI infrastructure, advanced medical devices, robotics, and autonomous vehicles. The firm maintains close ties with The Ohio State University’s ElectroScience Laboratory and Nanotech West Lab.

The company’s stated mission is to deliver advanced turnkey ICs that drive next-generation sensors and systems for mission-critical applications. Its STRIDE values — Staying Curious, Trust, Resilience, Innovation, Diversity, Excellence — reflect a culture built on multidisciplinary collaboration and proven technology validation.
